findings.title: Canonical Docker build fails: WASM build scripts hard-code .tools cargo path
findings.evidence: docker build target artifacts fails at Dockerfile.reproducible:68 (pnpm verify) with spawnSync /.tools/cargo/bin/cargo ENOENT; local pnpm verify passes only because ../.tools exists
findings.impact: CI, release workflow and build-reproducible.sh cannot produce canonical artifacts from HEAD
findings.detail:
- **Files:** [tooling/build-recovery-shamir-wasm.mjs:7-13](../../tooling/build-recovery-shamir-wasm.mjs#L7), [tooling/build-recovery-codex32-wasm.mjs:7-13](../../tooling/build-recovery-codex32-wasm.mjs#L7); compare [tooling/build-shielded-wasm.mjs:7-22](../../tooling/build-shielded-wasm.mjs#L7).
- **Observed:** `docker build --platform linux/amd64 --network host -f Dockerfile.reproducible --build-arg SOURCE_COMMIT=cdce70cb… --build-arg SOURCE_DIRTY=false --target artifacts .` fails at `Dockerfile.reproducible:68` (`RUN --network=none pnpm verify`) with `Error: spawnSync /.tools/cargo/bin/cargo ENOENT` raised by `build-recovery-shamir-wasm.mjs` right after "Generated pinned Dash Orchard browser WASM." (log `audit3/docker-full.log`, exit 1 after 62 s of the verify layer). Two attempts, same result.
- **Cause:** both new scripts compute `tools = <repo>/.tools` or `<repo>/../.tools` and then `cargo = resolve(tools, 'cargo/bin/cargo')` unconditionally. The Orchard script uses the same lookup but falls back to `CARGO_HOME`/`PATH` (`'cargo'`, `'wasm-bindgen'`) when the local toolchain directory is absent. In the container the toolchain lives at `/root/.cargo/bin` and `.tools` is excluded by `.dockerignore`, so `/.tools/cargo/bin/cargo` does not exist. Locally the same command succeeds only because `../.tools/cargo/bin/cargo` exists on this host (`pnpm verify` exit 0, 17:19 UTC).
- **Impact:** `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `full-wasm.yml`, `release.yml` and `./tooling/build-reproducible.sh` all run this Dockerfile; none can succeed on this commit, so no canonical artifacts, `verification-record.json`, attestations or release can be produced. The `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` and `SECURITY_AUDIT.md` statements that the Docker path defines release bytes are correct in design but not currently achievable.
- **Correction:** adopt the Orchard script's resolution (local `.tools` → `CARGO_HOME` → `PATH`), or factor one shared `resolveRustToolchain()` used by all three scripts. Add a unit test that runs the resolver with a fake root lacking `.tools` and asserts it yields `cargo`/`wasm-bindgen` from `PATH`. The bounded matrix smoke in the same Dockerfile never ran because the earlier layer failed.

findings.title: Selective Activity Viewer builds without Dash throw at startup (#viewer-build-fingerprint missing)
findings.evidence: --coins bitcoin and --coins ethereum builds raise 'Required Activity Viewer element is missing' in Chromium; dash-containing variants start
findings.detail:
- **Files:** [apps/activity-viewer/src/public-address-view.ts:46](../../apps/activity-viewer/src/public-address-view.ts#L46) (`required(document, '#viewer-build-fingerprint')`), [apps/activity-viewer/src/index.html:400-412](../../apps/activity-viewer/src/index.html#L400) (the fingerprint `<code>` lives inside the Dash "Viewer runtime" passport block), the Dash-fragment removal in the viewer build.
- **Observed:** `pnpm build:html -- --profile multi-chain --tool activity-viewer --coins ethereum` (and `--coins bitcoin`) builds successfully, but loading the artifact in Chromium raises `Error: Required Activity Viewer element is missing: #viewer-build-fingerprint.` before the controller starts; the coin selector shows only the selected coin and nothing else works. `--coins dash`, `--coins bitcoin,dash` and `--coins bitcoin,dash,ethereum` start normally (element count 2 vs 1 in the failing builds; the remaining occurrence is the JavaScript selector).
- **Impact:** the "Bitcoin-only" and "Ethereum-only" viewer compositions advertised by `docs/BUILD_MODULES.md` ("every supported coin alone" is part of the smoke matrix) ship as broken pages. The smoke matrix compiles them but never loads them.
- **Correction:** move the fingerprint element (and any other element that `required()` demands) out of the Dash-conditional fragment, or make the removal keep shared passport rows. Add a matrix smoke that opens at least one artifact per coin in a browser and asserts no page error (see §8).

findings.title: --output can overwrite canonical release artifacts with a selective build
findings.evidence: Dash-only Deriver written to dist/multi-chain-edition/key-derivation/Wallet_Key_Derivation_Tool.html (c9194584 -> d309be5e); contradicts docs/BUILD_MODULES.md
findings.detail:
- **Files:** [tooling/tool-feature-options.mjs:103-105](../../tooling/tool-feature-options.mjs#L103), [tooling/key-derivation-features.mjs:110-112](../../tooling/key-derivation-features.mjs#L110), [tooling/build-html-profiles.mjs:26-29](../../tooling/build-html-profiles.mjs#L26).
- **Observed:** `node tooling/build-html-profiles.mjs --profile multi-chain --tool key-derivation --coins dash --output dist/multi-chain-edition/key-derivation/Wallet_Key_Derivation_Tool.html` succeeded and replaced the canonical artifact (SHA-256 `c9194584…` → `d309be5e…`) while `dist/multi-chain-edition/SHA256SUMS` still listed the old digest. The reviewer rebuilt the canonical set afterwards (`pnpm build:html`), and the later Docker/local verify results refer to the restored bytes.
- **Doc conflict:** `docs/BUILD_MODULES.md` states "Custom builds are written below `dist/custom-builds/` and never replace canonical release artifacts" and "Canonical release filenames are reserved for complete edition builds". The reservation is only applied to the default path; an explicit `--output` bypasses it.
- **Correction:** when the composition is custom, reject `--output` paths inside `dist/<edition>/` or whose basename equals a canonical artifact name, or embed a "custom" marker in the artifact and make `verify-artifact-profiles` reject it under canonical names. Add a test.

findings.title: WASM bridge errors are primitive strings; Recovery UI shows generic messages
findings.evidence: ThresholdNotPassed { threshold: 3, n_shares: 2 } and MismatchedHrp thrown as strings; UI uses cause instanceof Error
findings.detail:
- **Files:** [packages/recovery-codex32-wasm/rust/src/lib.rs](../../packages/recovery-codex32-wasm/rust/src/lib.rs) and [packages/recovery-shamir-wasm/rust/src/lib.rs](../../packages/recovery-shamir-wasm/rust/src/lib.rs) (`JsValue::from_str`), [apps/key-derivation/src/ui/recovery-codex32.ts:99-126](../../apps/key-derivation/src/ui/recovery-codex32.ts#L99), [apps/key-derivation/src/ui/recovery-shamir.ts:45-60](../../apps/key-derivation/src/ui/recovery-shamir.ts#L45).
- **Observed (probe R4):** recovering BIP93 vector 3 with two of three shares throws the primitive string `Codex32 interpolation failed: ThresholdNotPassed { threshold: 3, n_shares: 2 }`; mixing an upper-case and lower-case share throws `… MismatchedHrp("ms", "MS")`. The UI catch blocks use `cause instanceof Error ? cause.message : 'Codex32 restoration failed.'`, so users see only the generic sentence. The Rust `{error:?}` Debug formatting is also not user-facing text.
- **Correction:** wrap bridge failures in `Error` inside `codex32.ts`/`shamir.ts` (or use `describeUnknownError`, which already handles strings) and map the known variants to plain sentences ("2 of 3 required shares were entered"). Add tests for the three cases above.

findings.title: CKD Shamir format has no secret digest; consistent tampered share recovers a different valid-looking phrase silently
findings.detail:
- **File:** [packages/recovery-backup/src/shamir.ts](../../packages/recovery-backup/src/shamir.ts).
- **Observed (probe R7):** a raw share whose payload byte was flipped and whose 4-byte SHA-256 trailer was recomputed recovers a *different* 32-byte secret without any error, and that entropy always converts to a valid-looking BIP39 phrase. The per-share checksum protects against accidental corruption only; nothing binds the shares to the secret (SLIP-39 uses a digest share for this; BIP93 has the same limitation by design).
- **Assessment:** not a vulnerability (an adversary who can alter a share can also withhold it), but a recovery-safety gap for the stated audience: a wrong-but-consistent set silently produces a plausible phrase. The documentation calls the format "checksummed" without stating this.
- **Correction:** in a versioned format update include a truncated digest of the secret (SLIP-39 style) or an HMAC share; until then document the limitation next to the "verify with a standard wallet" advice. Keep the positive property found here: word shares are 27–39 words and never validate as BIP39 mnemonics (`validateMnemonic` false), so they cannot be confused with a seed phrase.

findings.title: Watch-only-only scanner build retains hidden seed-mode markup/copy although seed modules are excluded
findings.detail:
- **Observed:** `--tool discovery-scanner --coins bitcoin,ethereum --features watch-only-discovery` excludes the seed code (no BIP39 wordlist, no `mnemonicToSeed`, no Dash provider URLs; the generated Worker allowlist and dispatcher contain exactly `ping`, `utxo.addresses`, `evm.accounts`, `address.history`; the Public Input Boundary label is present) — but the iframe still contains the hidden `#seed-source-tab`, the `#single-mnemonic`, `#batch-mnemonics` and `#batch-passphrases` textareas and "Secret Vault"/"mnemonic" copy. `docs/BUILD_MODULES.md` says removing a feature "deletes its marked HTML fragment".
- **Correction:** strip the seed-mode fragment as done for the Deriver panels, and add an artifact check that a watch-only-only build contains no `mnemonic` control ids.

findings.title: Flaky Firefox acceptance: Multi-Chain Deriver #coin 'dash' !== 'bitcoin' once in four runs
findings.detail:
- **Observed:** in the first full `verify-browser-files.mjs` run (17:10 UTC) the Firefox 153 `multi-chain/key-derivation` case failed with `'dash' !== 'bitcoin'` at [tooling/verify-browser-files.mjs:307](../../tooling/verify-browser-files.mjs#L307), immediately after `#crypto-self-test-status.passed`. Two further full runs and the other agent's earlier runs on previous commits passed (16/16). Chromium never failed.
- **Assessment:** intermittent; root cause not established (candidates: Firefox restoring a `<select>` state, or the assertion racing the `populateCoinSelect`/default-adapter initialisation in [apps/key-derivation/src/ui/inputs.ts:50](../../apps/key-derivation/src/ui/inputs.ts#L50), which appends options without setting `select.value`). Record it as a flake; set the default explicitly after populating and make the runner wait for it.

observations.title: Documentation drift: BROWSER_ACCEPTANCE 38 vs 42 cases; SECURITY_AUDIT latest review predates modular work; connect-src https:; upstream /home/runner string
observations.detail:
1. `docs/BROWSER_ACCEPTANCE.md:33` still says "38-case matrix"; the runner now produces 42 runs across 11 case families (`recovery-backup-roundtrips` was added).
2. `SECURITY_AUDIT.md` names the 2026-09-12 re-verification of `d978dd4d` as the latest review; the six commits that introduced shared packages, selective builds and the recovery codecs were unreviewed until this report.
3. `docs/BUILD_MODULES.md` "operations for excluded coins are absent from its code" holds for the Worker allowlist/dispatcher; the vault-side `NetworkBoundaryClient` still carries all 14 operation names (harmless: the Worker rejects them).
4. `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` describes the connected tools as "HTTPS enabled"; their CSP is `connect-src https:` (any host) while providers are fixed in code. Not a contradiction, but see §7 recommendation on host pinning.
5. The `/home/runner/work/platform/...` string inside the Viewer/Scanner artifacts comes from the upstream Dash `wasm-sdk` glue (`file:///home/runner/...` fallback URL), not from this host; `example.invalid` is a placeholder host. Neither is a path leak of this repository.
